answer: The land office froze terrace lots in the hillside orchard that crowns the knoll; a live identity binds to only one lot. Enrollment publishes a soil-core isotopic fingerprint and the lot's boundary hash with a single signing key. Later an optical pass, lit to a published comet ephemeris, matches canopy geometry and the core assay, then demands a nonce signature from that key. A second claimant on the same lot is slashed and the crop seized. A hundred fake names require buying, assaying, and imaging a hundred scarce lots, so attacker cost stays at least linear.
